headline: Rangers’ Alberts Smits out week-to-week with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports Alberts Smits is out week-to-week with an upper-body injury. The No. 5 pick in June's draft made the Rangers out of camp and still hasn't recorded his first NHL point.

That's a rookie learning on the job, and the numbers look like it. In 17 games he has 0.88 expected goals and none scored, so a bit of bad luck, and the Rangers have taken 47.9% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, about six points worse than without him. Ordinary for an 18-year-old on the third pair at 14:35 a night. New York (10-7-1, 53% of the expected goals) can absorb this better than the Sean Durzi absence. In the one game since Smits went out, Matthew Robertson moved in beside Morrow; watch whether that holds tonight in Edmonton.
